parsed.explanation: Claim 3.2 takes an arbitrary minimal transversal T of C and forms π(T), which is defined only for finite sets; nothing in the premises forces T finite. The objection's example C={{2,x_n}} is a genuine intersecting antichain with the infinite minimal transversal {x_n}, so hypothesis (iii) as stated is not proved for all minimal transversals. This matters: Step 4's final contradiction applies (a) and (iii) to the possibly infinite set I∪Z_ω, obtaining a minimal transversal T that is then asserted finite; only the Case A use involves a finite set I∪Z_s. Hence the finiteness route (L6.2's role) is unsupported, and no other passage establishes finiteness. Repair requires new argument (lemma-level).
